signals.title: There are rare bikes, and then there's the Yoshimura Tornado!
signals.summary: Limited to just 50 bikes worldwide, the Yoshimura Tornado is one of the rarest bikes money can buy, and this one has just gone up for sale. If you were to ask your riding buddies to name a famous motorcycle tuner, the most likely name they’d muster up would be Yoshimura. Hideo “Pops” Yoshimura built his reputation alongside the growth of Japanese brands on the global stage, and went on to become a name synonymous with Suzuki. 2003 saw the brand branch out, as it created a motorcycle that would go on to become two-wheeled folklore: the Tornado S-1. Built from the innards of a first-generation Suzuki GSX-R1000, just 50 examples of this mythical beast were ever produced, making it rarer than both the Ducati Desmosedici and Honda RC213V-S. And there is more going on here than simply some aftermarket fairings and a sticker kit. Yoshimura went to town with the GSX-R1000, updating and upgrading the bike at a forensic level. Internally, the engine features a thinner head gasket, high-compression pistons, beefed-up valve springs, and hot cams. The exhaust is a bespoke four-into-one system, topped off by a beautiful Tri-Oval end can. The chassis is also boosted thanks to Ohlins fully adjustable suspension and upgraded brakes. All told, the Tornado produced around 170bhp, more than five more than the donor bike it’s based on. But this bike’s allure isn’t the performance gap between it and the bike it is based on. signals.title: Adventure motorcycles continue to steer the UK’s positive sales numbers
signals.summary: Adventure motorcycle registrations grew by 41 per cent in July compared to the same month in 2025. 2026 has so far been a strong year for motorcycle sales in the UK, which continued in July, according to the latest statistics provided by the Motorcycle Industry Association (MCIA). The adventure segment has played a key role in the ongoing growth month-to-month vs 2025, and that was also the case in July. Adventure motorcycle registrations were up by a staggering 41.8 per cent compared to the same month in 2025. Year-to-date, adventure motorcycle sales are also holding strong, with an overall increase of 26.2 per cent. The naked motorcycle segment also flourished in July, with registrations growing by 24.5 per cent compared with July 2025. Not far behind that was the touring segment, with monthly registrations growing by 18.2 per cent. Year-to-date registrations for the entire motorcycle segment have grown by 16.1 per cent, while YTD scooter sales are up by 15.4 per cent. In terms of individual models, the best-performing bike in July 2026 was the Honda CB125F, which sold 185 units in the naked category. That was then followed by the CB1000GT which sold 141 units, while third place went the way of the GB350S, meaning Honda finished the month with the three best-selling motorcycles. signals.title: It’s official: research suggests e-scooters are more dangerous than motorcycles
signals.summary: New research comparing more than 15,000 trauma cases suggests e-scooter riders suffer significantly more head and internal injuries than motorcyclists. E-scooter riders are 3.5 times more likely to suffer a traumatic brain injury than motorcyclists when they end up in serious crashes, according to a new study comparing injury data from across England and Wales. The research, published in Scientific Reports, looked at 15,247 patients admitted with moderate-to-severe trauma between 2020 and 2022. The group included 580 e-scooter riders, 7027 motorcyclists and 7640 pedal cyclists, with the surgeon, David Bodansky, at the head of the investigation. The results make uncomfortable reading for anyone who sees an e-scooter as a relatively harmless alternative to a motorcycle or bicycle. Among adult riders suffering serious injuries, the risk of traumatic brain injury was 3.45 times higher for e-scooter riders than motorcyclists, while the risk was 1.74 times higher than for cyclists. E-scooter riders were also more likely to suffer internal organ injuries, with a 46 per cent higher risk than motorcyclists, while vascular injuries involving arteries and veins were more than three times as common. There is, however, an important distinction to be made regarding the figures. The study isn't saying that someone riding an e-scooter is 3.5 times more likely to crash or suffer a brain injury than someone riding a motorcycle. signals.title: Norton’s new Manx R superbike already has a one-off custom edition
signals.summary: Norton has revealed a new partnership with Peaceful Research that has led to one of the most flashy Manx R liveries you’re likely to see. Norton’s ongoing resurgence has already given us the 206bhp Manx R, the naked Manx variant, and the Atlas and Atlas GT adventure bikes. However, a flashy, one-off version of the Manx R has now been revealed. The one-off model is a result of Norton’s new collaboration with Peaceful Research, while a limited-run of clothing was also revealed on August 7, at 7pm BST. The clothing collection features a hoodie, t-shirt and cap, although it’s the bold-looking Manx R that unquestionably steals the show. Dressed in a metallic pink and deep purple colourway, this one-off model was on display at last weekend’s British MotoGP at Silverstone. The new colourway is also very different to any of the standard Manx R colours, which include Trophy Silver, Matrix Black, Celestial Grey, Aqua Green, Carbon, and Glacier Blue options. For those that don’t know, Peaceful Research is a contemporary motorsport and lifestyle goods company, and the collaboration between the two companies was forged to reimagine Norton’s racing heritage through the lens of Peaceful Research. It’s not been confirmed whether the one-of-one custom build will go up for sale at any stage, and at what price, although it would likely blow past the British brand’s entry price point of £20,250 for the base Manx R model. signals.title: Ducati bidder wants MV Agusta too... and Triumph out of Moto2!
signals.summary: The group behind a €2.5bn bid for Ducati has outlined what it would do if the deal goes through, including replacing Triumph in Moto2 and making the entire operation Italian! Patritalia has reiterated its bid to buy Ducati from the Audi/Volkswagen Group, claiming that its €2.5bn offer remains on the table indefinitely and outlining what it would do if it gets its hands on the Bologna-based manufacturer. And if it’s CEO and founder is to be believed, it isn't stopping at Ducati. The Italian group says MV Agusta is also among its targets, with the stated aim of returning both brands, and other unnamed Italian companies, to Italian ownership. Patritalia says this is central to its founding philosophy and that Ducati and MV Agusta are of interest specifically because they are currently foreign-owned. Quite how far that philosophy would extend is where things get interesting. In a lengthy social media statement aimed at correcting what Patritalia describes as "distorted" reporting about its plans, the company says that if it acquires Ducati, its "Italian Patriotism" would be applied at every level of the business. Most notably, it says its companies would be "always and only" made up of Italians, regardless of the skills foreign employees might bring. That appears to mean a Ducati workforce that is exclusively Italian, from the workshop floor sweeper, right up to the president. Quite how that would work in practice is less clear. signals.title: Ducati’s new V2-powered Monster claims special Red Dot award
signals.summary: Ducati celebrates a major win for the new V2-powered Monster, which follows the same path as Suzuki's GSX-8T and GSX-8TT models. Ducati’s 2026 Monster, which uses the company’s all-new 890cc V2 engine platform, has won the prestigious Red Dot award in the Product Design category for 2026. You might be interested in reading our 2026 Ducati Monster review . Ducati's win in the Red Dot Product Design category was achieved, in part, through the Italian brand's continued evolution of the Monster platform, which is now in its fifth-generation. Speaking about the latest version of the Monster, Ducati said: "Introduced in 2025, the new Monster carries this heritage into the future through an entirely new project, combining lightness, technology and a contemporary, instantly recognisable design language. More compact, essential and sporty, the new Monster recalls the elements that have defined its identity since the very beginning: the headlight framed by the “shoulders” of the bison-back tank, the one-piece seat, and the short, lightweight tail section." This major win for Ducati comes after other brands have also tasted similar success in 2026, including Honda and Suzuki . Honda celebrated further Red Dot success through its electric WN7, which recently backed up its iF Design honour with an award win in the Red Dot product design category. signals.title: Honda CB1000GT secures top spot in the UK sales charts
signals.summary: Honda’s new CB1000GT sold more units in July 2026 than some of the UK’s most popular motorcycles from the last two years. The new Honda CB1000GT has become one of the UK’s best-selling motorcycles for the first time since its launch earlier this year. You might be interested in reading our Honda CB1000GT review . The CB1000GT was revealed at the 2025 EICMA show in Milan, Italy, alongside the new V3R 900 E-Compressor, and the brand’s expanded E-Clutch line-up which now includes the XL750 Transalp, CB750 Hornet, NX500, CBR500R and CB500 Hornet. Although a sports tourer at heart, the CB1000GT also takes after its naked sibling, the CB1000 Hornet, blending Fireblade-derived engine performance with the comfort needed for longer journeys. Where things become particularly interesting with regards to July’s best-performing motorcycles in the UK, is the category that the CB1000GT has fallen under. The sports tourer has been positioned alongside more adventure-focused motorcycles based on the statistics provided by the Motorcycle Industry Association (MCIA). This also means that the CB1000GT sold more units than BMW’s R1300 GS, which has often been the top-performing adventure model in recent months. In fact, the R1300 GS had not been toppled by another motorcycle since February, when Honda’s NC750X sold the most units for that month. signals.title: Cremona round officially renamed as EICMA strikes new deal with WorldSBK
signals.summary: The 2026 Cremona WorldSBK event has taken on a new name as part of a wider collaboration between EICMA and WorldSBK. EICMA has announced a new collaboration with the WorldSBK Championship that’s set to take centre stage at two major events in 2026. The new agreement means that round ten of the 2026 WorldSBK Championship, which takes place at the Cremona circuit on 25–27 September, will now officially be called the EICMA Italian Round. This means that guests attending the event on behalf of EICMA will be able to enjoy a bespoke WorldSBK hospitality programme at Cremona. Additionally, both organisations are set to collaborate on a dedicated communications campaign that will be featured on digital and social media channels as part of the build up to the race, and November’s exhibition in Milan, Italy. The expanded partnership also means that WorldSBK will join MotoGP in a series of initiatives under the company’s ‘Road to EICMA’ banner. For those that have already bought tickets to the 2026 EICMA show, or plan to buy tickets, a €10 (around £8.50) discount is available on tickets to the WorldSBK race weekend at Cremona. WorldSBK is also set to bring its ‘The Garage’ hospitality experience to the 83rd edition of the EICMA show, which will offer fans, partners, and stakeholders a more immersive experience of the championship. signals.title: Zero Motorcycles is offering cash rewards for new riders, here’s how it works
signals.summary: Zero Motorcycles has revealed a new Rider Bonus scheme across several of the company’s motorcycles and LS1 scooter, and here’s how it works. Zero Motorcycles is offering newly qualified riders the chance to earn cashback when they buy one of the company’s motorcycles or LS1 scooter, although the cashback amounts vary depending on the model. The new Rider Bonus scheme ends on December 31, 2026, and is available across the DSR/X and DS sport-tourers, as well as the SR/F and S nakeds. The cashback amount for any of these models is £400. However, if customers select the brand’s LS1 scooter or XE dirt bike, they will instead receive a reimbursement of £200. To be in with a chance of activating the cashback reward, new riders will need to have purchased their Zero motorcycle within three months of completing their CBT, A1, A2 or full A motorcycle license. According to Zero Motorcycles, the offer only applies to “new motorcycles and scooters from model years 2025 and 2026 that have never been previously registered”. Additionally, motorcycles or scooters that have been ordered by a Zero Motorcycles dealer as demonstration models are not included in the offer. The motorcycle or scooter must be purchased from an authorised Zero Motorcycles dealer in any of the following countries; Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, France, Sweden, Spain, Italy, the UK and Ireland. signals.summary: Wuling Kejar TKDN Mobil Listrik 60 Persen pada 2027 TANGERANG, KOMPAS.com Wuling Motors memastikan akan mengikuti ketentuan Tingkat Komponen Dalam Negeri (TKDN) untuk mobil listrik yang berlaku di Indonesia. Pabrikan asal China tersebut menargetkan kandungan lokal kendaraan listriknya bisa mencapai 60 persen pada 2027. Marketing Director Wuling Motors Ricky Christian mengatakan, pihaknya saat ini tengah mengecek seluruh komponen yang digunakan pada mobil listrik untuk memastikan kesiapan memenuhi ketentuan tersebut. Menurut dia, sejumlah komponen mobil listrik Wuling sudah menggunakan produk yang diproduksi atau bersumber dari dalam negeri. Salah satunya adalah baterai dan komponen interior. "Lagi dicek semua komponen, tapi beberapa kan emang sudah jalan ya. Seperti baterai dan interior," kata Ricky.
